1: Vivy Prototype by Tappei Nagatsuki and Eiji Umehara (Seven Seas) is a thoughtful science fiction story about an AI learning what it means to have a heart. Vivy is an android singer whose only dream is to make people happy with her songs. Then an AI named Matsumoto arrives from a hundred years in the future with a warning: a war between humans and AI is coming, and Vivy must help stop it. Readers who enjoy sci-fi with real feeling will find a lot here.
5: Kuroko's Basketball by Tadatoshi Fujimaki (Viz Media) is an energetic sports comedy about teamwork and rivalry on the court. Taiga Kagami, a powerhouse player back from the US, joins the new team at Seirin High. There he meets Tetsuya Kuroko, a quiet boy so easy to overlook that he seems invisible, who was secretly the sixth man of a legendary middle school team. This omnibus edition collects the story in big two-in-one volumes, great for fans of fast games and big personalities.
7: RWBY: The Official Manga by Bunta Kinami (Viz Media) is an action fantasy based on the popular animated series. Ruby Rose is a young girl with a giant scythe and a big dream of becoming a Huntress who protects the world from monsters called Grimm. When she is invited to Beacon Academy two years early, she joins a team with three very different girls. Fans of the show and newcomers alike will enjoy the fast fights and friendships.
10: Liar Liar by Haruki Kuou (Yen Press) is a clever comedy about bluffing your way to the top. Hiroto Shinohara transfers to Academy Island, a school city where students settle everything through games and duels. On his first day he wins a match against the school's top player by pure trickery, and suddenly everyone believes he is the strongest student there. Now he has to keep the lie going. Readers who like mind games and quick-witted heroes will have fun.
12: Log Horizon by Mamare Touno (Yen Press) is a fantasy adventure set inside an online game. When thirty thousand Japanese players suddenly find themselves trapped in the world of the MMORPG Elder Tale, the game becomes real life. Shiroe, a quiet strategist who usually works alone, teams up with his old friends to figure out how to survive and how to build a society in this new world. It is a great pick for readers who like smart planning as much as battles.
14: Di Gi Charat by Koge-Donbo (Broccoli Books) is a silly, cute comedy full of cat ears and gags. Dejiko is a catgirl princess from the planet Di Gi Charat who comes to Earth determined to become a star. She takes a job at a game and anime shop in Akihabara, along with her friends, and causes chaos wherever she goes. Fans of short, cheerful gag stories and early-2000s otaku culture will enjoy it.
18: Dojinwork by Hiroyuki (Anime Works) is a light comedy about the world of self-published comics. Najimi Osana is a college student who decides she wants to become a doujin artist and sell her own comics at conventions, even though she has a lot to learn. With help and teasing from her friends, she tries to break into the scene. Readers curious about fan comics and convention culture will find plenty to laugh at.
20: Scrapped Princess by Ichiro Sakaki (Tokyopop) is a fantasy adventure about a girl the whole world wants gone. Pacifica Casull was born a princess, but a prophecy said she would destroy the world, so she was thrown away as a baby. Now fifteen and raised by a kind family, she is on the run from the kingdom's assassins, protected by her adoptive siblings Shannon and Raquel. It is a good fit for readers who like road-trip fantasy with heart.
21: Lost Lad London by Shima Shinya (Yen Press) is a quiet, stylish mystery set in modern London. Al is a university student who rides the Tube home one night and finds a bloody knife in his coat pocket, tying him to the murder of a well-known politician. A detective named Ellis offers him a deal, and the two set out to find the real killer together. Readers who enjoy moody, character-driven crime stories will be drawn in.
23: Love in Focus by Yoko Nogiri (Kodansha) is a gentle shojo romance about photography and first love. Mako Kohinata loves taking pictures, so she moves to a boarding school known for its photo club. There she is reunited with Kei, her childhood friend, and meets the cool, talented Ryo. As she learns to see the world through her camera, she also starts to understand her own heart. Fans of sweet, low-drama romance will enjoy it.
24: Love in Hell by Reiji Suzumaru (Seven Seas) is a goofy supernatural comedy about the afterlife. Rinne Inamura dies an embarrassing death and lands in Hell, where he must serve out a sentence of hundreds of years. His guide through the punishments is Koyuki, a cute and strict demon warden. Rinne decides that Hell might not be so bad after all. Readers who like silly humor and odd-couple romance will have a good time.
27: Your Name by Makoto Shinkai (Yen Press) is a heartfelt romantic drama based on the hit animated film. Mitsuha is a high school girl in a small mountain town who dreams of life in Tokyo, while Taki is a Tokyo boy busy with school and a part-time job. One day they start waking up in each other's bodies. At first it is confusing and funny, but soon they want to meet for real. Fans of the movie will love seeing the story on the page.
30: ElfQuest: The Grand Quest by Wendy and Richard Pini (DC Comics) is a classic fantasy adventure, collected here in a compact, manga-sized format. Cutter is the young chief of the Wolfriders, a tribe of elves who live with their wolf companions. When humans burn their forest home, the tribe must leave and set out across a strange and dangerous world in search of a new place to live. It is a great choice for readers who love sweeping fantasy and found family.
31: Mark of the Succubus by Ashly Raiti (Tokyopop) is a supernatural romance with a dark, playful edge. Maeve is a young succubus in training, and for her final test she must go to the human world and lead one mortal into darkness. She chooses Aric, a quiet high school boy, but the more she gets to know him, the harder her job becomes. Fans of forbidden romance and paranormal stories will enjoy it.
33: MBQ by Felipe Smith (Tokyopop) is a gritty, darkly funny comic about chasing your dream in Los Angeles. Omar is a young artist who wants to make it big drawing manga, but for now he is broke and working a miserable fast-food job. Between bad bosses, strange coworkers, and a city that does not care, he keeps trying to get his big break. Readers who like edgy humor and underdog stories will find it memorable.
36: Fairy Cube by Kaori Yuki (Viz Media) is a dark fantasy with gothic art and a lot of emotion. Ian is a boy who has always been able to see fairies and spirits, a gift that has made his life lonely. When a mysterious spirit steals his body and his place in the world, Ian has to fight his way back to protect Rin, the girl he loves. Fans of Kaori Yuki's moody, beautiful style will feel right at home.
38: Final Fantasy Type-0 Side Story: The Ice Reaper by Takatoshi Shiozawa (Yen Press) is a fantasy war story set in the world of the Final Fantasy Type-0 game. Kurasame is a talented young cadet in Akademeia, a school that trains magic users to fight for their nation. As war breaks out, he and his closest friends are sent into battle, where they must face the cost of being soldiers. Fans of the game and of military fantasy will want to read it.
39: Fire Force by Atsushi Ohkubo (Kodansha) is a high-energy action story about firefighters with supernatural powers. In a world where people can suddenly burst into flames and turn into monsters called Infernals, special fire brigades exist to stop them. Shinra Kusakabe, a boy with the power to make fire from his feet, joins Special Fire Force Company 8 to become a hero. This omnibus edition collects several volumes in each book, perfect for fans of big fights and stylish art.
40: Seven of Seven by Yasuhiro Imagawa (ADV) is a lighthearted sci-fi comedy about one girl who suddenly becomes seven. Nanako Suzuki is a busy student preparing for high school entrance exams when an accident splits her into seven copies of herself. Each one has a different personality, from cheerful to grumpy to shy, and they all have to share one life. Readers who like zany school comedies will have fun with it.
44: Bloom Into You Anthology: Regarding Saeki Sayaka by Hitoma Iruma (Seven Seas) is a tender yuri romance novel set in the world of the Bloom Into You manga. Sayaka Saeki is the serious, hardworking vice president of the student council. This story looks back at her life, from the experience in middle school that taught her about her own heart to her quiet feelings for the student council president, Touko. Fans of the manga will appreciate this deeper look at Sayaka.
49: Off*Beat by Jen Lee Quick (Tokyopop) is a quiet drama about curiosity, secrets, and first feelings. Tory Blake is a smart, lonely teenager in New York who notices a new boy, Colin, moving in across the street. He becomes obsessed with figuring out who Colin is and why his family seems to be hiding something. Readers who enjoy slow-building, thoughtful stories with a touch of mystery will like it.
51: Gimmick! by Youzaburou Kanari (Viz Media) is an action drama set in the movie business. Kohei Nagase is a gifted young special effects makeup artist who works on films and TV. His skill with masks, prosthetics, and disguises is so good that people keep coming to him for help with problems far from the set, and he often ends up using his craft to set things right. Readers who are curious about behind-the-scenes movie magic will enjoy it.
52: Cardcaptors by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a bright, magical adventure adapted from the beloved Cardcaptor Sakura. Sakura Kinomoto is a cheerful fourth grader who opens a strange book in her father's library and accidentally releases the magical Clow Cards. With help from Kero, the cards' small guardian, she must capture every card before it causes trouble. It is a lovely pick for younger readers and longtime magical girl fans.
53: Train Man: Densha Otoko by Hidenori Hara (Viz Media) is a sweet romantic comedy based on a true internet story. A shy young otaku stands up to a drunk man bothering a woman on a train. Afterward, she sends him a thank-you gift, and he has no idea what to do next. He turns to an online message board, where strangers offer advice and cheer him on as he tries to ask her out. It is a warm, funny read for anyone who has felt awkward in love.
54: Giant Spider & Me: A Post-Apocalyptic Tale by Kikori Morino (Seven Seas) is a cozy slice-of-life story set after the end of the world. Nagi is a young girl living alone in the mountains, hunting and growing food to survive. One day she meets Asa, a giant spider who turns out to be gentle and curious, and the two start living together. Readers who enjoy calm stories about food, nature, and unlikely friendship will love it.
57: .hack//Another Birth by Miu Kawasaki (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi mystery novel series set in the world of the .hack games. Akira Kunisaki's older brother falls into a coma after playing The World, a popular online game. Determined to find out what happened, she logs in herself as a sword-wielding character named BlackRose. Fans of the games will enjoy seeing the story from her side.
58: Penguindrum by Kunihiko Ikuhara (Seven Seas) is a strange, emotional drama novel based on the anime Mawaru Penguindrum. Brothers Kanba and Shoma Takakura live with their younger sister Himari, who is very sick. On a trip to the aquarium she collapses, then is brought back by a mysterious penguin hat that demands the brothers find something called the Penguindrum. It is a great choice for readers who like surreal stories with heart.
59: The NPCs in This Village Sim Game Must Be Real! by Hirukuma (Seven Seas) is a cozy fantasy story about a game that may be more than a game. Yoshio is a shut-in who spends his days playing a village-building sim. As he watches over the villagers and helps them survive, he starts to suspect that they are real people living in a real world. Readers who enjoy gentle stories about building a home and caring for others will like it.
60: 7th Time Loop: The Villainess Enjoys a Carefree Life Married to Her Worst Enemy! by Touko Amekawa (Seven Seas) is a fantasy romance with a clever, capable heroine. Rishe has lived her life six times over, as a merchant, a maid, a knight, and more, and she always dies at twenty. On her seventh loop she just wants to relax, but then Prince Arnold Hein, the man who killed her in a past life, asks her to marry him. Fans of smart heroines and slow-burn romance will be hooked.
61: Clockwork Planet by Yuu Kamiya and Tsubaki Himana (Kodansha) is a sci-fi adventure set on a world made entirely of gears. After the Earth died, it was rebuilt as a giant machine. Naoto Miura is a high schooler who is bad at school but has an amazing ear for machinery. One day a broken automaton crashes through his roof, and when he repairs her, he is pulled into a fight to save the planet. It is a great fit for readers who love clockwork and big ideas.
62: Rokka: Braves of the Six Flowers by Ishio Yamagata (Yen Press) is a fantasy mystery about heroes who cannot trust each other. When the Demon God stirs, six warriors are chosen to stop it. Adlet Mayer, who calls himself the strongest man in the world, is one of them. But when the heroes gather, there are seven, which means one of them is a fake. Readers who like whodunits mixed with sword-and-sorcery action will enjoy it.
64: Boogiepop by Kouhei Kadono (Seven Seas) is a moody urban fantasy light novel series that helped shape the genre. At a Japanese high school, students whisper about Boogiepop, a figure said to be a shinigami who appears to people at the height of their beauty. When students start to disappear, the story unfolds from many different viewpoints. Readers who enjoy puzzle-like storytelling and eerie atmosphere will find it fascinating.
65: Full Metal Panic! by Shoji Gatoh (J-Novel Club) is an action comedy light novel series about a soldier who has no idea how to be a normal teenager. Sousuke Sagara is an elite fighter for a secret military group. His new mission is to pose as a high school student in Tokyo and protect Kaname Chidori, a girl who is in danger for reasons she does not know. Fans of giant robots, school comedy, and a little romance will love it.
66: Log Horizon by Mamare Touno (Yen Press) is the original light novel series behind the anime and manga. When thirty thousand Japanese players are suddenly trapped inside the online game Elder Tale, the game world becomes their real life. Shiroe, a quiet and clever strategist, begins working out how to survive and how to make this new world a better place. It is a great pick for readers who enjoy smart planning, politics, and game-world adventure.
69: Deadpool: Samurai by Sanshiro Kasama (Viz Media) is a wild action comedy that brings Marvel's famous antihero to Japan. Deadpool wants to join the Avengers, so he signs up as a member of the Samurai Squad in Tokyo. There he battles villains, causes chaos, and talks to the reader every chance he gets. Fans of Deadpool's humor and of over-the-top manga action will both get a kick out of it.
74: Vampire Kisses: Blood Relatives by Ellen Schreiber (Tokyopop) is a gothic romance based on the popular Vampire Kisses novels. Raven is a goth girl in a sleepy small town who has always felt out of place. Her boyfriend Alexander is a vampire, and she is happy with him, but trouble arrives when his strange cousin Jagger comes to town. Readers who enjoy spooky romance and dark, pretty art will like this series.
75: Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid: Fafnir the Recluse by coolkyousinnjya (Seven Seas) is a laid-back comedy spinoff of Miss Kobayashi's Dragon Maid. Fafnir is a grumpy, dangerous dragon who lives in the human world at the apartment of Takiya, Kobayashi's otaku coworker. He spends most of his days playing video games and grumbling about humans. Fans of the main series will enjoy this quiet, funny look at one of its oddest characters.
79: Occultic;Nine by Chiyomaru Shikura (J-Novel Club) is a supernatural mystery light novel about rumors that turn out to be real. Yuta Gamon is a high school student who runs a blog about the paranormal, though he does not really believe in any of it. When he and a group of strangers are drawn into a strange event in their city, the occult stories he collects start to look a lot less like fiction. Readers who like twisty mysteries will enjoy it.
84: Run Away With Me, Girl by Battan (Kodansha) is a quiet, grown-up yuri romance. Midori and Maki dated in high school, but Maki ended things. Ten years later, they run into each other as adults. Midori has never stopped loving her, but Maki is working an office job and planning a life that does not include Midori. Readers who like honest, bittersweet love stories will be moved by it.
85: Haven't You Heard? I'm Sakamoto by Nami Sano (Seven Seas) is a deadpan school comedy about the coolest guy alive. Sakamoto is a high school student who does everything with perfect style, from answering a question in class to dealing with bullies. The other students try to trip him up, but he always turns every problem into another chance to look amazing. Readers who like quick, silly humor will laugh out loud.
86: Akuma no Riddle: Riddle Story of Devil by Yun Kouga (Seven Seas) is an action thriller about a class full of assassins. Tokaku Azuma, a young assassin, transfers to the Black Class at an all-girls academy. Every other girl in the class is also an assassin, and they all have the same target: their kind classmate Haru Ichinose. Tokaku starts to wonder if she would rather protect Haru instead. Fans of tense action and complicated bonds between girls will enjoy it.
88: Genshiken: Second Season by Kio Shimoku (Kodansha) is a funny, warm comedy about a college otaku club. The original members of the Society for the Study of Modern Visual Culture have mostly graduated. Now the shy artist Ogiue is club president, and she must welcome a new group of members, including a boy named Hato who likes to dress as a girl. Readers who love manga about fandom, friendship, and growing up will feel right at home.
89: Cowboy Bebop by Yutaka Nanten (Tokyopop) is a stylish sci-fi action manga based on the classic anime. In the year 2071, Spike Spiegel and Jet Black are bounty hunters who travel the solar system aboard their ship, the Bebop, always chasing their next payday. Along the way they pick up a strange crew, including the con artist Faye Valentine. Fans of the show will enjoy these new adventures with its cast.
93: The Cain Saga by Kaori Yuki (Viz Media) is a gothic mystery set in Victorian England. Cain Hargreaves is a young earl with a dark family history and a deep knowledge of poisons. With his loyal servant Riff by his side, he investigates strange and deadly cases among the upper class. Readers who love gothic drama, gorgeous art, and twisted family secrets will be drawn in.
94: The Dreaming by Queenie Chan (Tokyopop) is a creepy horror mystery set in the Australian bush. Twin sisters Amber and Jeanie arrive at a remote boarding school surrounded by thick forest. They soon hear stories of students who wandered into the woods and never came back, and the school seems to be hiding something. It is a good pick for readers who enjoy slow, eerie ghost stories.
96: Jyu-Oh-Sei by Natsumi Itsuki (Tokyopop) is a sci-fi survival story about two twins left on a dangerous world. Thor and Rai are young brothers who live comfortable lives on a space colony until their parents are killed. The twins are then sent to Chimera, a prison planet full of deadly plants and violent gangs. To survive, they must learn the rules of this harsh place. Readers who enjoy intense sci-fi with mystery will be hooked.
97: The Voynich Hotel by Seiman Douman (Seven Seas) is a strange, darkly funny mix of crime, horror, and romance. Taizo is a Japanese man hiding out at the Voynich Hotel on a small island in Southeast Asia. The hotel is home to an odd cast of guests and staff, including witches, criminals, and killers. Readers who like weird, offbeat stories with a dark sense of humor will enjoy it.
99: Twin Spica by Kou Yaginuma (Vertical) is a gentle, moving story about chasing your dreams. When Asumi Kamogawa was a little girl, Japan's first manned rocket crashed into her town. Years later, she wants to become an astronaut more than anything, and she applies to the new Tokyo Space School. Readers who enjoy quiet coming-of-age stories with real heart will love it.
102: Hi Score Girl by Rensuke Oshikiri (Square Enix Manga) is a nostalgic romantic comedy set in the arcades of the 1990s. It is 1991, and Haruo Yaguchi is a sixth grader who lives for fighting games. His world is turned upside down when he is beaten by Akira Oono, a quiet rich girl who turns out to be an amazing player. Fans of retro games and slow-burn romance will both enjoy it.
103: Beast Complex by Paru Itagaki (Viz Media) is a collection of short stories set in the same world as Beastars. In a city where meat-eating and plant-eating animals live together, each chapter follows two very different animals whose lives come together. Some stories are sweet and some are tense, but all of them show the tricky balance between predators and prey. Fans of Beastars and newcomers alike will find it easy to dive into.
104: Hitohira by Idumi Kirihara (Aurora) is a heartfelt school story about finding your voice. Mugi Asai is a shy first-year who has trouble speaking up. She is pushed into joining the drama club, where the bold upperclassman Nono sees something special in her. As Mugi learns to act, she also learns to be braver. Readers who like quiet, encouraging stories about friendship will enjoy it.
105: Barrage by Kohei Horikoshi (Viz Media) is a sci-fi adventure from the creator of My Hero Academia. Astro is a poor boy living in a run-down part of a planet called Industria. He happens to look exactly like the planet's prince, so the prince asks Astro to take his place and become the hero the kingdom needs. Fans of Horikoshi's later work will enjoy seeing his early style.
108: Afro Samurai by Takashi Okazaki (Titan Manga) is a stylish, gritty action story mixing samurai and hip-hop. Whoever wears the Number One headband is said to be the strongest fighter in the world, and the Number Two headband gives its owner the right to challenge them. As a boy, Afro saw his father killed by the gunman who took the Number One headband. Now grown, he sets out for revenge. Fans of bold art and nonstop sword fights will enjoy it.
109: The Hentai Prince and the Stony Cat by Sou Sagara (Yen Press) is a romantic comedy about wishes that go wrong. Yoto Yokodera is a high school boy who is tired of hiding his true, slightly pervy thoughts behind a polite face. He makes a wish at a stone cat statue to lose his facade. At the same time, a quiet girl named Tsukiko wishes she could stop showing her feelings, and both wishes come true. It is a silly, sweet read for fans of school comedy.
111: Clover by CLAMP (Tokyopop) is a stylish sci-fi fairy tale told with striking art. Kazuhiko is a former soldier who is called back for one last job: to deliver a girl named Sue to a place called Fairy Park. Sue is a Clover, a girl with incredible magical power who has been kept locked away. As they travel, Kazuhiko learns what Sue truly wants. Readers who love CLAMP's elegant style will want this in their collection.
112: Soulless by Gail Carriger (Yen Press) is a witty steampunk romance based on the popular novels. Alexia Tarabotti is a sharp-tongued spinster in Victorian London, and she has a secret: she has no soul, so her touch cancels supernatural powers. When a rude vampire attacks her at a party, she accidentally kills him, which brings her to the attention of Lord Maccon, a werewolf investigator. Fans of romance, humor, and parasols will have fun.
113: Ex-Yakuza and Stray Kitten by Riddle Kamimura (Seven Seas) is a sweet slice-of-life comedy about a tough guy and a tiny cat. Kenji is a gruff former yakuza who has just gotten out of prison and is trying to live a quiet life. When he finds a little stray kitten, he decides to take her home and name her Kiki. Readers who love gentle, funny stories about pets will be smiling the whole way through.
116: Club 9 by Makoto Kobayashi (Dark Horse) is a lighthearted comedy about a country girl in the big city. Haruo is a cheerful young woman from a small town who moves to Tokyo for college. To make ends meet, she takes a job as a hostess at a fancy club, where her honest, naive personality gets her into all kinds of funny situations. Readers who enjoy upbeat, slice-of-life comedy with a retro feel will like it.
118: Touring After the Apocalypse by Sakae Saito (Yen Press) is a calm, quietly lovely road-trip story. Yoko and her android companion Airi ride their motorcycle across a Japan where nearly all the people are gone. They visit famous places, now empty and overgrown, and make the best of whatever they find. Readers who enjoy peaceful travel stories and soft, wistful moods will love it.
120: Satsuma Gishiden by Hiroshi Hirata (Dark Horse) is a hard-hitting historical samurai drama. In 18th-century Japan, the ruling Tokugawa shogunate punishes the proud Satsuma clan by forcing its samurai to carry out a costly and dangerous flood-control project. The story follows the struggles and anger of these warriors under crushing pressure. Readers who like serious historical fiction and powerful, gritty art will appreciate it.
121: Magia Record: Puella Magi Madoka Magica Side Story by Magica Quartet (Yen Press) is a magical girl fantasy set in the world of Madoka Magica. Iroha Tamaki is a magical girl who cannot remember the wish she made to get her powers. Following rumors that magical girls can be saved in Kamihama City, she heads there to find answers and meets new magical girls along the way. Fans of the original series will enjoy this new chapter.
123: Kobato. by CLAMP (Yen Press) is a gentle fantasy romance with a bit of mystery. Kobato Hanato is a cheerful, clumsy girl on a special mission: she must heal the wounded hearts of people around her and collect them in a little bottle. Guiding her is Ioryogi, a grumpy creature who looks like a plush toy dog. Readers who enjoy warm, magical stories with heart will love it.
125: The Devil Does Exist by Mitsuba Takanashi (CMX) is a classic shojo romantic comedy. Kayano is a sweet high school girl who works up the courage to write a love letter to her crush. But the letter ends up in the hands of Takeru, the troublemaking son of the principal, who decides to tease her. Before long, their arguments start to turn into something more. Fans of old-school shojo romance will enjoy it.
127: Castle in the Sky Film Comic by Hayao Miyazaki (Viz Media) retells the classic Studio Ghibli adventure using full-color frames from the film. Pazu is a hardworking mining boy who sees a girl float down from the sky. Her name is Sheeta, and she wears a mysterious crystal that pirates and soldiers are both chasing. Together, the two set out to find the legendary floating city of Laputa. It is a lovely way for fans of all ages to revisit the movie.
128: I Am Here! by Ema Toyama (Del Rey) is a sweet shojo story about being noticed. Hikage is a shy middle school girl who is so quiet that her classmates barely know she exists. Her only outlet is a blog where she shares her feelings with online friends. When she is suddenly assigned to class duties with Hinata, a kind and popular boy, she has a chance to finally be seen. Readers who have ever felt invisible will connect with it.
131: Revolutionary Girl Utena by Chiho Saito (Viz Media) is a dreamy, dramatic shojo fantasy. When Utena Tenjou was young, a prince comforted her, and she decided she wanted to become a prince herself. Now at Ohtori Academy, she wears a boy's uniform and stands up for her friends. When she challenges a student council member to a duel, she wins Anthy, the mysterious Rose Bride, and is drawn into a strange series of duels. Fans of the anime will love it.
134: The Other World's Books Depend on the Bean Counter by Yatsuki Wakatsu (Yen Press) is a boys' love fantasy with a very practical hero. Seiichi Kondo is an ordinary office worker who is accidentally summoned to another world along with a young woman meant to be its Saint. Left on his own, he takes a job in the royal accounting office and starts fixing the kingdom's messy finances. Readers who enjoy slow-burn romance and clever, hardworking leads will like it.
136: Under the Oak Tree by Kim Suji (Inklore) is a romantic fantasy based on a popular web novel. Maximilian Croyso is a shy noblewoman who has always been treated harshly by her family. She is married off to Riftan Calypse, a knight of low birth, who leaves for war right after the wedding. Three years later, he comes home a hero and wants to take her to his lands. Fans of slow-burn romance and lush art will be swept away.
137: The Complete Chi's Sweet Home by Konami Kanata (Vertical) is an adorable comedy about a kitten finding a new family. Chi is a tiny gray kitten who gets lost on a walk with her mother. A young boy named Yohei and his parents find her and take her home, even though pets are not allowed in their apartment. Each short chapter shows Chi exploring her new world. Perfect for cat lovers and readers of all ages.
138: Vampire Princess Miyu by Narumi Kakinouchi (Studio Ironcat) is a gothic horror story with a sad, beautiful mood. Miyu looks like a young girl, but she is really a vampire with a special duty: to find Shinma, demons who have escaped into the human world, and send them back to darkness. She is joined by Larva, her silent masked guardian. Fans of moody, classic shojo horror will enjoy it.
150: Kill la Kill by Ryo Akizuki (Udon) is a wild action comedy based on the hit anime. Ryuko Matoi is a fierce girl carrying half of a giant scissor blade, searching for the person who killed her father. Her search brings her to Honnouji Academy, a school ruled by the powerful student council president Satsuki Kiryuin and her elite students in special uniforms. Fans of big, loud action and bold characters will enjoy it.
155: Bocchi the Rock! Side Story: Kikuri Hiroi's Heavy-Drinking Diary by Aki Hamazi and Kumichou (Yen Press) is a comedy spinoff of Bocchi the Rock! Kikuri Hiroi is a talented bassist in an indie band, but she is also always broke and almost never sober. This series follows her chaotic daily life, from shows and band practice to borrowing money from her friends. Fans of the main series will enjoy spending more time with this lovable mess.
158: Aharen-san Is Indecipherable by Asato Mizu (Yen Press) is a cute, offbeat school romantic comedy. Raido is a high school boy with a serious face and a big imagination. He sits next to Aharen, a tiny girl who has no sense of personal space; sometimes she stands far away, and sometimes she is right up against him. As he tries to figure her out, the two slowly become close. Readers who like gentle, quirky humor will enjoy it.
170: Battle Royale by Koushun Takami and Masayuki Taguchi (Yen Press) is an intense survival thriller based on the famous novel. Shuya Nanahara and his junior high classmates think they are on a school trip, but they are taken to an island and told they must fight until only one of them is left alive. As friends and rivals face the choice to fight or trust each other, the tension never lets up. This is for older readers who like dark, gripping stories.
175: Once Upon a Witch's Death by Kenu Amearare (Yen Press) is a gentle fantasy about making the most of the time you have. Meg Raspberry is an apprentice witch who learns she has only one year left to live. The only way to save herself is to gather a thousand tears of joy from the people she helps. Readers who enjoy warm, emotional stories with a touch of magic will be moved by it.
179: Spice and Wolf by Isuna Hasekura and Keito Koume (Yen Press) is a cozy fantasy romance about trade and travel. Lawrence is a traveling merchant who finds a girl with wolf ears and a tail sleeping in his wagon. She is Holo, a wolf goddess of the harvest, who wants to return to her northern home. The two set out on the road together, trading wits as well as goods. This collector's edition is a lovely way to enjoy the series.
194: Blue Lock: Full Color Selection by Muneyuki Kaneshiro and Yusuke Nomura (Kodansha) presents the hit soccer manga in full color. After his high school team loses, striker Yoichi Isagi is invited to Blue Lock, a training program meant to create the world's greatest striker. He and three hundred other young players must compete against each other, and only one will come out on top. Fans of intense sports stories will love seeing it in color.
196: MARS by Fuyumi Soryo (Kodansha) is a classic shojo romance and drama, now in a 30th anniversary edition. Kira is a shy art student who spends most of her time drawing. Rei is a popular, reckless motorcycle racer with a bad reputation. When Kira gives Rei a sketch, the two start to form an unlikely bond that changes both of their lives. Readers who like emotional love stories with depth will appreciate it.
197: Witch Hat Atelier by Kamome Shirahama (Kodansha) is a gentle fantasy adventure with gorgeous, detailed art. Coco is a girl who has always dreamed of being a witch, but in her world, only those born with magic can use it. When she sees the witch Qifrey drawing a spell, she learns a secret that changes her life. This Grimoire Edition is a special collector's version, perfect for fans who love the series.
213: Aoashi by Yugo Kobayashi (Titan Manga) is a sports drama about soccer and growing up. Ashito Aoi is a talented but rough-around-the-edges middle school player from a small town in Ehime. When Tatsuya Fukuda, the coach of a top Tokyo youth team, sees his raw talent, he invites Ashito to try out. Ashito heads to the big city with a big dream. Fans of sports manga who like a focus on tactics and teamwork will enjoy it.
215: Solo Leveling: Ragnarok by Daul (Ize Press) is an action fantasy sequel to the hit Solo Leveling. Years after Sung Jinwoo saved the world, his son Suho is living an ordinary life as a college student. But when new threats appear, Suho discovers that he may have inherited some of his father's powers. Fans of the original series will want to see what comes next.
218: PTSD Radio by Masaaki Nakayama (Kodansha) is a chilling horror anthology. Each short chapter tells a different spooky story about ordinary people who run into something they cannot explain. Little by little, the stories connect around an eerie figure known as Ogushi-sama. Readers who enjoy unsettling, bite-sized horror will find it hard to put down, and this omnibus edition collects several volumes in each book.
219: Air Gear by Oh! Great (Kodansha) is a high-energy action story about street skating. Itsuki Minami, called Ikki, is a tough middle school boy who loves a good fight. When he discovers Air Treks, motorized inline skates that let riders fly through the streets, he is pulled into a world of skating gangs and battles. This omnibus edition collects several volumes in each book, perfect for fans of fast action and bold art.
220: Legend of the Galactic Heroes by Yoshiki Tanaka (Haikasoru) is a classic space opera novel series about war and politics. In the far future, two powers have been at war for over a century. Reinhard von Lohengramm is an ambitious young admiral of the Galactic Empire, while Yang Wen-li is a reluctant but brilliant commander of the Free Planets Alliance. Readers who love big, thoughtful sci-fi with clever battles will be hooked.
222: Butterflies, Flowers by Yuki Yoshihara (Viz Media) is a romantic comedy for grown-up readers. Choko Kuze comes from a wealthy family that lost everything. Now she is an office worker at a real estate company, where her strict boss, Masayuki Domoto, turns out to be the servant boy who once looked after her. At work he is harsh, but after hours he still calls her milady. Readers who like office romance with lots of humor will enjoy it.
